summary: This change adds a new audit-trail patch file (ai-os/patches/quality-gate-run-gate-timeout-2026-07-27.diff) documenting a fix applied directly to the live, untracked /opt/veridian/scripts/quality-gate.sh, following the same recorded-patch convention established by the 2026-07-26 OOM-cap fix; the underlying fix itself is sound and well-scoped, replacing the unbounded eval "$cmd" in run_gate() with timeout -k 30 "$GATE_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS" bash -c "$cmd" (default 900s, overridable via env var), correctly detecting timeout/kill exit codes (124/137) and logging them into the gate's tail output so a hang now surfaces as a normal failed gate through the existing auto-fix-then-blocked pipeline instead of stalling the worker forever undetected behind the periodic-checkpoint heartbeat exemption; the same wrapping is applied to the dependency-install step for consistency. The diff is purely additive (one new file, no deletions), touches no migrations/schema/auth/permission/billing/security paths and no .github/workflows/**, so it is correctly tier1.
issues: Minor/non-blocking: the install-step timeout is piped into `tail -20` (`timeout ... $PKG_MGR install 2>&1 | tail -20`), so the script's exit status there reflects tail, not timeout -- a timeout/kill on install won't be distinguishable from success by exit code. This mirrors the pre-existing script's behavior (install's exit code was never checked before this patch either), so it isn't a regression, but it does mean the install-step timeout only bounds wall-clock time without actually surfacing an install timeout as a failure the way run_gate() now does for other gates.

Minor: switching from `eval "$cmd"` to `bash -c "$cmd"` (via timeout) runs the gate command in a subshell rather than the calling shell's context -- functionally equivalent for the typical self-contained lint/build/test invocations this script runs, but any gate command that relied on mutating the parent script's shell variables/environment (none observed in the visible diff context) would silently stop doing so.
